messages: 3	Three Years Later	three-years-later	Sophia never expected to see Dominic again. But when she walks into Kane Industries for a job interview, the past comes rushing back—along with feelings she thought she'd buried.	The last person I expected to see at Kane Industries was Dominic Kane himself. Three years hadn't changed him—same intense dark eyes, same commanding presence that once made my knees weak. Still made them weak, apparently.
"Sophia." My name on his lips sent a shiver down my spine. "I didn't know you were the candidate."

I stood frozen in the doorway of the executive conference room, my carefully prepared interview notes suddenly feeling useless in my hands. Of all the companies in Manhattan, of all the positions I could have applied for, I'd somehow ended up here. At his company. Interviewing for a role that would put me directly in his orbit again.
"Mr. Kane," I managed, proud that my voice didn't shake. "I didn't realize you'd be conducting the interview personally."
Something flickered in his eyes—pain, regret, hunger. "It's Dominic. It's always been Dominic, Sophia. Don't do that. Don't pretend we're strangers."

But that's exactly what we were now, weren't we? Three years ago, we'd been everything to each other. Three years ago, I'd thought he was the one. Then he'd chosen his career over us, accepted a position in London without even discussing it with me, and I'd been left to pick up the pieces of my shattered heart alone.
"I should go," I said, already turning toward the door. "This was a mistake."

"Wait." He crossed the room in three strides, his hand catching my wrist. The touch was electric, familiar, devastating. "Please. Just... give me five minutes. If you still want to leave after that, I won't stop you."

I should have walked out. Should have protected myself from the man who'd broken my heart so thoroughly that it took me two years to even consider dating again. But something in his voice—a vulnerability I'd never heard before—made me pause.
"Five minutes," I agreed, pulling my wrist free. I needed distance. Needed to think clearly. "That's all you get."

He nodded, gesturing to the conference table. We sat across from each other, the polished wood a barrier between us. It felt symbolic somehow—this expensive table representing all the ways we'd failed to communicate, all the things left unsaid.
"You look good," Dominic said quietly. "More than good. You look... happy."

"I am happy." It wasn't entirely true, but I'd learned to fake it well enough. "I have a good life in Boston. Good friends, good job. This position would be a step up, but I don't need it. I'm fine on my own."
"I know you are." His jaw tightened. "You were always strong enough to be fine on your own. That was never the question."

"Then what was the question, Dominic?" The words came out sharper than I intended, three years of buried hurt rising to the surface. "Because from where I stood, you made your choice pretty clear. London was more important than us. Your career was more important than what we had."
"That's not—" He broke off, running a hand through his dark hair in frustration. "God, Sophia, is that really what you thought? That I chose London over you?"

"What else was I supposed to think?" I stood, unable to sit still anymore. "You got the offer and accepted it within a week. You didn't ask me to come with you. You didn't even discuss it with me. You just... decided. And I was supposed to what? Uproot my entire life to follow you across the ocean on the off chance you might want me there?"

"I didn't ask you to come because I knew you wouldn't." He stood too, his voice rising to match mine. "Your mother had just been diagnosed. Your sister was starting college. Your entire family was in New York, and I wasn't going to be the selfish bastard who asked you to choose between them and me."
The words hit me like a physical blow. "You never gave me the chance to choose."

"Because I knew what you'd choose!" He moved around the table, closing the distance between us. "And I couldn't—I couldn't be the reason you resented me five years down the line. I couldn't be the man who took you away from your family when they needed you most. So I made the choice for you. I went to London, and I let you go, and it was the biggest fucking mistake of my life."
My breath caught. "Dominic—"

"I came back for you," he continued, his voice rough with emotion. "Six months later, when I realized I couldn't live without you, I came back. But you'd already moved to Boston. You'd blocked my number, deleted me from social media. You made it very clear you wanted nothing to do with me."

"Because you broke my heart!" The admission tore out of me. "You made me believe we had a future, and then you left. Do you have any idea what that did to me? How long it took me to feel whole again?"

"I know." He reached for me, his hands cupping my face with a gentleness that made my eyes sting. "I know, and I'm so fucking sorry, Sophia. I thought I was doing the right thing. I thought I was being noble, putting your needs first. But all I did was hurt us both."
A tear slipped down my cheek, and he caught it with his thumb. "Why didn't you fight for me?" I whispered. "Why didn't you try harder?"

"Because I'm an idiot." His forehead pressed against mine, and I could feel him trembling. "Because I convinced myself you were better off without me. Because I was a coward who couldn't face the possibility that you might actually choose me, and then I'd have to live up to that. I'd have to be the man you deserved, and Sophia, I wasn't sure I could be."
"You were always that man," I said, my hands coming up to grip his wrists. "You were everything I wanted. Everything I needed. And you just... left."

"I know." He pulled back just enough to look at me, his dark eyes swimming with regret. "And if I could go back and do it differently, I would. I'd get down on my knees and beg you to come with me. I'd turn down London entirely. I'd do whatever it took to keep you. But I can't change the past, Sophia. All I can do is tell you the truth now."
"Which is?"

"That I never stopped loving you." The words hung in the air between us, raw and honest. "Three years, a dozen cities, more women than I care to admit trying to fill the void you left—none of it mattered. None of them were you. And when I saw your resume come across my desk, saw that you were applying to work here, I knew it was a sign. A second chance I don't deserve but desperately want."
My heart hammered against my ribs. "Dominic, I can't—I can't just pick up where we left off. Too much has happened. Too much time has passed."

"I'm not asking you to." His hands slid down to my shoulders, then my arms, his touch gentle but grounding. "I'm asking for a chance to earn your trust again. To prove that I'm not the same man who let you go. I'm asking for coffee, for dinner, for the opportunity to show you that what we had wasn't just young love or convenient timing. It was real, Sophia. It is real. And if you feel even a fraction of what I'm feeling right now, then please—give me a chance."

I should have said no. Should have protected my heart, walked out of that conference room, and never looked back. But standing there, with Dominic's hands on my arms and his eyes pleading with mine, I couldn't deny the truth.
I'd never stopped loving him either.
"One chance," I said, my voice barely above a whisper. "You get one chance, Dominic. If you hurt me again—"

"I won't." He pulled me into his arms, holding me so tightly I could barely breathe. "I swear to you, Sophia, I won't. I'll spend every day proving that I'm worth the risk. That we're worth the risk."
I buried my face in his chest, breathing in the familiar scent of him—cedar and spice and something uniquely Dominic. "I'm scared," I admitted.
"So am I." His lips pressed against my hair. "But I'm more scared of letting you walk away again. More scared of spending the rest of my life wondering what if."
I pulled back to look at him, and the intensity in his gaze stole my breath. "What about the job? I can't work here if we're—"

"Then don't work here." He said it without hesitation. "I'll help you find something else, something better. I'm not letting company policy stand between us again. You're more important than any job, Sophia. You're more important than anything."
The declaration should have terrified me. Instead, it felt like coming home.
"Kiss me," I whispered, and his eyes darkened with heat.
"Are you sure?"
"I'm sure."

He kissed me like a man starved, like I was oxygen and he'd been drowning. His mouth was hot and demanding, his hands sliding into my hair, tilting my head to deepen the kiss. I melted into him, three years of longing and heartache dissolving in the heat of his embrace.

When we finally broke apart, both breathing hard, he rested his forehead against mine. "Come home with me," he said, his voice rough with need. "Let me show you how much I've missed you. Let me make up for every day we've been apart."

I should have been sensible. Should have insisted we take things slow, rebuild trust before jumping into bed. But looking into his eyes, feeling the solid warmth of him against me, I couldn't bring myself to care about should.
"Yes," I breathed, and his answering smile was pure sin.

What followed was a blur of heated kisses and desperate touches as we made our way to his penthouse. Dominic made love to me with a passion that left me breathless, whispering promises against my skin and showing me, with every touch and every kiss, that he meant every word he'd said.
Afterward, we lay tangled together in his bed, Manhattan glittering beyond the floor-to-ceiling windows. His fingers traced lazy patterns on my bare shoulder, and I'd never felt more content.
"I love you," he said softly. "I never stopped, and I never will."
I turned to look at him, this complicated, brilliant man who'd broken my heart and was now carefully piecing it back together. "I love you too," I admitted. "Even when I hated you, I loved you."

"Then stay." His hand cupped my face, thumb brushing across my cheekbone. "Move back to New York. Move in with me. Let's do this right this time, Sophia. Let's build the life we should have had three years ago."
It was too fast, too soon. We had so much to work through, so many conversations still to have. But looking into his eyes, seeing the love and hope and determination there, I found myself nodding.
"Okay," I whispered. "Let's try."
His kiss was soft, sweet, full of promise. "I won't let you down," he said. "Not this time. Not ever again."
And wrapped in his arms, with the city lights painting shadows across his features, I let myself believe him.
